question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI participants, with structural MRI as the shared channel. P-273's DISFC is multimodal: 3D sMRI, demographic/cognitive scores and 49 SNPs, with a 48-month horizon. P-198 feeds five FreeSurfer cortical-thickness covariates into a two-state Markov model followed by logistic regression, with transition to AD by a second visit about two years after baseline. Same task, population class and shared channel. The added predictors, horizon, features and model differ; the rule allows these.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (and accuracy with accuracy), both from internal 10-fold CV on ADNI.

figures.P-273: Trimodal DISFC AUC 0.962 (fold SD 0.041), accuracy 92.92%, on a CV set of 238 MCI (91 pMCI / 147 sMCI, derived from 94/158 overall minus the 3/11 in the ADNI-3 test set). Hanley-McNeil: SE = 0.0144; interval [0.934, 0.990]. MRI-only unimodal arm read from Fig. 4B, calibrated against the printed trimodal bars to about +-0.004: AUC about 0.802, Hanley-McNeil with 91/147 SE = 0.0310, interval [0.741, 0.863]. MRI-only accuracy about 0.758, Wilson n = 238: [0.700, 0.808].
figures.P-198: Cortical-thickness model, stratified 10-fold CV (one cycle), 721 MCI (188 converters / 533 sMCI): AUC 0.78 +- 0.08, accuracy 0.75 +- 0.02 (fold SDs; no interval printed). Hanley-McNeil for 0.78 with 188/533: Q1 = 0.78/1.22 = 0.6393; Q2 = 2*0.6084/1.78 = 0.6836; SE^2 = [0.1716 + 187*(0.6393-0.6084) + 532*(0.6836-0.6084)]/(188*533) = 45.95/100204 = 0.000459; SE = 0.0214; interval [0.738, 0.822]. With the fold SD as the spread: [0.623, 0.937]. Accuracy 0.75, Wilson n = 721: [0.717, 0.780].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. P-273's Fig. 4B unimodal MRI model, cross-validated with identical settings, is P-198's input condition (MRI only). Its AUC of about 0.802 lies inside P-198's interval [0.738, 0.822], and P-198's 0.78 lies inside P-273's MRI-only interval [0.741, 0.863]; two-sample z = (0.802-0.78)/sqrt(0.0310^2+0.0214^2) = 0.58. The accuracies agree too (0.758 vs 0.75, z = 0.25). Both directions hold across the whole reading range of the bar (0.795-0.806). P-273's own ablation shows that its advantage over MRI-only models comes from the cognitive/clinical inputs: MRI-only about 0.80, MRI+clinical about 0.94, trimodal 0.962. No figure matches the horizon (48 months vs about 2 years), but the channel-matched figures already agree.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. P-273's 0.962 is below 0.97 and has a small (n = 14) ADNI-3 test. P-198's 0.78 comes from 721 subjects. Note that P-198's top-5 covariates were chosen by Relief on the whole dataset before cross-validation, which is a possible optimism, but its figure is not near ceiling. Checked against P-273 pages 6-7 and P-198 pages 2-5.
reason: The recorded AUCs (0.962 vs 0.78) differ beyond uncertainty, but the 0.962 comes from P-273's trimodal model, which uses cognitive scores and genotypes. P-273's own MRI-only arm (about 0.80 AUC, about 0.76 accuracy) agrees with P-198's MRI-only 0.78 AUC and 0.75 accuracy in both directions. The papers' own data dissolve the gap and P-273 shows its source, so condition 3 fails. The ledger's 'AUC 0.56' for P-198 is its no-covariate baseline, not its best model.

quotes.quote: On the cross-validation set, our model achieved superior results for predicting MCI conversion within 4 years (AUC, 0.962; accuracy, 92.92%; sensitivity, 88.89%; specificity, 95.33%)
For each participant, we considered 14 clinical features at baseline, including demographic data (age, sex, education) and cognitive assessments, as listed in Table 1.
As shown in Fig. 4B, the DISFC model using trimodal data achieved the best performance. We also observed that bimodal models outperformed unimodal models overall.
The unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal models were cross-validated with identical settings. Each bar represents the mean value across folds for each metric
using λ to predict whether a test patient will transition to AD within the next two years, given the outcome of the first visit.
The dataset includes 721 MCI individuals, 533 of whom were categorized as having stable MCI (sMCI)
